prompt: Explain to a beginner how a bicycle turns pedalling into movement.
opening: Pedals start a connected chain reaction.
subject: bicycle drivetrain
development: Follow force from pedals through the chain to the driven wheel.
visualDirection: Consistent ordinary bicycle; moving close-ups illustrate the mechanism, not evidence.

beats.title: Start at the pedals
beats.narration: Pushing the pedals turns the front chainring.
beats.subject: bicycle pedals turning
beats.action: Close view of pedals and chainring turning together.

beats.title: Follow the chain
beats.narration: The moving chain turns gears at the rear wheel.
beats.subject: bicycle chain rear gears
beats.action: Follow the chain moving onto the rear sprocket.

beats.title: Meet the ground
beats.narration: The driven wheel pushes against the ground, moving you forward.
beats.subject: bicycle rear wheel riding
beats.action: Side view of a bicycle moving along level ground.

prompt: Show a beginner how to fold a sheet of paper in half neatly.
opening: Match the edges before you crease.
subject: hands folding paper
development: Align opposite edges, hold them together, then press a crease.
visualDirection: Close framing of the same hands and plain sheet; no tools needed.

beats.title: Bring the edges together
beats.narration: Bring one short edge over to meet the other.
beats.subject: hands folding paper
beats.action: Hands bring the short edges of a sheet together.

beats.title: Check both corners
beats.narration: Adjust both corners until the edges line up.
beats.subject: hands aligning paper corners
beats.action: Close view of the aligned corners before pressing.

beats.title: Press the fold
beats.narration: Hold the edges together and press along the fold.
beats.subject: hands creasing folded paper
beats.action: Hands press a straight crease; finish on aligned paper edges.

prompt: Tell a tiny fictional story about a turtle returning a library book.
opening: The turtle was one day late.
subject: turtle carrying book
development: A worried turtle makes the return and discovers a welcoming library.
visualDirection: A small green turtle with a red book in a cosy illustrated town.

beats.title: One determined reader
beats.narration: He carried his book through the rain.
beats.subject: turtle carrying book rain
beats.action: The small green turtle shelters a red book while walking.

beats.title: An open door
beats.narration: At the library, he nearly turned back.
beats.subject: turtle library doorway
beats.action: The turtle hesitates at a warmly lit library entrance.

beats.title: A welcome return
beats.narration: The librarian smiled and saved him a dry seat.
beats.subject: turtle library reading
beats.action: The same turtle settles with his book beside a warm lamp.

prompt: Tell a tiny joke about a robot caring for a cactus.
opening: The robot took plant care seriously.
subject: robot cactus
development: A dutiful robot misunderstands the cactus rather than explaining gardening.
visualDirection: One small box-shaped robot beside a potted cactus; dry comic timing.

beats.title: A careful inspection
beats.narration: It scanned every spike for signs of distress.
beats.subject: robot inspecting cactus
beats.action: The robot slowly inspects a small potted cactus.

beats.title: A generous offer
beats.narration: Then it offered the cactus a hug.
beats.subject: robot reaching cactus
beats.action: The robot opens its arms toward the cactus and pauses.

beats.title: A revised policy
beats.narration: Personal space became its highest priority.
beats.subject: robot backing from cactus
beats.action: The same robot carefully backs away from the cactus.

prompt: Compare two fictional bags: Trail holds 20 litres and weighs 400 grams; Metro holds 20 litres and weighs 800 grams. Which is lighter for the same capacity?
subject: two backpacks
development: Compare identical capacity, then the supplied weights; finish with the requested choice.
visualDirection: Two distinct backpacks shown consistently; narration carries supplied quantities, no invented features.

beats.title: The same capacity
beats.narration: Both Trail and Metro hold twenty litres.
beats.subject: two backpacks side by side
beats.action: Show two backpacks side by side at the same scale.

beats.title: Different weights
beats.narration: Trail weighs four hundred grams; Metro weighs eight hundred.
beats.subject: backpacks on weighing scale
beats.action: Illustrative view of backpacks being weighed; no generated numbers.

beats.title: Choose the lighter bag
beats.narration: Choose Trail for equal capacity with less weight.
beats.subject: lightweight backpack carrying
beats.action: A person picks up the selected backpack.
